PullRequest.Title: editor: move Modern UI tab scrollbars to the top
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #341954

Move the horizontal scrollbar to the top of Modern UI editor tabs, aligning Pill and Connected styles while leaving Legacy unchanged. For Connected tabs, this keeps the scrollbar from cutting between the selected tab and the editor body. It overlays the existing header without changing tab-row heights or shifting the content below.

The regular editor and Agents window use matching thumb thickness and rounded ends. Existing hover/scroll reveal, auto-hide, and explicit scrollbar size and visibility settings are preserved. Legacy tabs, breadcrumbs, editor-content scrollbars, and panel/status-bar spacing stay unchanged.

### Visual evidence

Final tab-style comparison, captured from the current PR head: **Legacy stays below; Modern UI Pill and Connected use the top.** Scrollbars are deliberately visible to show placement. These are component-fixture captures, not native-window recordings.

**Dark 2026**

![Dark 2026: Legacy scrollbar below; Modern UI Pill and Connected scrollbars above](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb129d13-fda6-4328-b156-3aaf2a874442)

**Light 2026**

![Light 2026: Legacy scrollbar below; Modern UI Pill and Connected scrollbars above](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57fd8b65-cb1c-46e8-a9e1-e14277cff9a4)

### Try it

1. Enable Modern UI, select either Pill or Connected editor tabs, and open enough files to overflow the tab strip.
2. Hover or scroll the tabs in the editor and Agents window. The scrollbar appears at the top with matching thickness, then hides when idle; the tabs and content do not move.
3. Turn on Wrap Tabs and resize the editor area. Wrapped rows remain stable, with the bottom active tab connected to the editor.
4. Check the existing scrollbar size and visibility settings. Disable Modern UI to confirm Legacy tabs retain their bottom scrollbar.

### Validation

- `npm run compile` — passed, including client type-checking.
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/editorPart.test.ts --browser chromium --reporter dot` — 95 passed.
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/browser/media/tabs.css` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts src/vs/sessions/test/browser/editorPart.test.ts src/vs/workbench/test/browser/componentFixtures/editor/tabs.fixture.ts` — passed.
- Final Legacy/Pill/Connected comparison fixtures rendered and inspected in default dark/light and both high-contrast themes. Real Agents stylesheet tests verify generated thumb paint, 3px/10px sizes, and exclusions for Legacy, breadcrumbs, and editor content.
- Native Connected-tab validation: matching painted thumbs and hover/drag colors, hidden when idle, with no header or body movement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Overflowing Modern UI Pill or Connected tabs in the regular workbench during initial layout, hover reveal, scrolling, and dragging
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing tab-strip layout creates the scrollbar; browser style resolution applies the three new rules and paint/compositing positions the existing track at the top. Hover/scroll progress does not wait on any new JavaScript or external operation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of open editor groups, not number of tabs: the direct-child selector matches one horizontal scrollbar per group after overflow. Tab count only determines whether the pre-existing scrollbar is needed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer UI thread; no new asynchronous work, queue, fan-out, or concurrency. One existing horizontal scrollbar is affected per editor group.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. Cold and warm behavior differ only through normal browser CSS/style caches; the diff adds no keys, misses, invalidation policy, or repeated fetch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the production diff is entirely static CSS, and the selector scope and scrollbar implementation show a single absolutely positioned, layer-hinted existing thumb per matching group.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style-resolution and paint cost varies by browser and editor-group count, but each rule changes only constant-size properties on an already-existing track/thumb and does not add layout-dependent reads or nodes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Moving the absolute track with `top`, applying border radius, and changing the Agents pseudo-element inset may cause the normal constant repaint but introduces no scaling layout work or hot-path JavaScript.

Scenarios.Scenario: Overflowing Modern UI editor tabs in the Agents window, including hover/drag thumb painting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing Agents scrollbar pseudo-element is painted after the Modern UI override changes its inset from 1px to 0 and moves the track to the top. No work outside style resolution and painting is required before interaction proceeds.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is one scrollbar/pseudo-element per overflowing editor group; selector matching does not fan out per open tab.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer UI thread; one existing scrollbar and pseudo-element per editor group, with no parallel tasks or boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache or remote data. Standard browser style caching applies equally before and after the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the existing Agents rule already creates the pseudo-element; this PR only overrides its inset and radius/position properties.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Paint timing is not measured, but the changed painted area is bounded to the existing scrollbar track and remains constant for a given group width.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff neither creates an additional painted layer nor adds per-frame script/layout work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Legacy tabs, breadcrumbs, and editor-content scrollbars while Modern UI classes are absent or outside the tab-row structure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser selector matching rejects these surfaces; their existing scrollbar layout and paint path remains unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unaffected by tab, breadcrumb, or editor-content cardinality because the new selector requires a Modern UI editor tab-row ancestry and direct scrollbar structure.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; selector scope is directly established by the changed CSS and tested structures.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change on this scenario.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and every diff page. The production change consists of three bounded CSS overrides on existing editor-tab scrollbars; tests and fixtures do not ship on product interaction paths. Tracing regular-workbench, Agents, and excluded scrollbar scenarios found no new expensive boundary, repeated work, retention, concurrency burst, forced layout, or scaling paint mechanism, so no performance finding was submitted.
